message.content:
In this C++ repository (D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-state-propagation), there is a transaction system with a "dry run" execution option meant to let callers validate a transaction without committing to the database. The bug: transactions triggered via standard user channels are being permanently written to the database even when dry run is requested.

I need you to investigate and report back (do NOT modify any code, this is research only):

1. Find the definition of the execution options / transaction options struct/class that contains the "dry run" flag (search for terms like "DryRun", "dry_run", "ExecutionOptions", "TransactionOptions", etc.)
2. Find where transactions are triggered from "standard user channels" (e.g. API handlers, request handlers, command handlers, controllers) — trace how the dry run flag is passed in from the entry point.
3. Trace the full call chain of how this options struct (or the dry run flag specifically) propagates from the entry point down to the actual point where the transaction is committed/written to the database.
4. Identify precisely where in that call chain the dry run flag is lost or ignored — e.g. a function that takes the options but doesn't forward them to the next call, a default-constructed options object created partway through instead of forwarding the real one, an overload that drops the parameter, a conditional that checks the flag incorrectly, etc.
5. Also identify where the actual "commit to database" / "write to database" logic lives and how it currently decides whether to skip writing (if it does at all).

For each relevant file, give me the exact file path and line numbers with the relevant code snippets. Be thorough — trace every hop in the call chain from entry point to database write. Report in detail so I can make the fix myself without needing to re-explore.
